limitations: Running jobs are nonpreemptive; only queued jobs are replaced. Preemptive latest-look service can behave differently.
The confidence-threshold monotonicity gate uses E68's expected fixed empirical rates. Production estimates can fluctuate between looks.
Jobs remain identical-cost FIFO work and the pending queue holds only the latest look. Variable cost, priority, cancellation overhead, and multiple metric services remain unmodeled.
Coalescing is outcome-independent and conservative here. Data-dependent look selection would require separate optional-stopping control.
All earlier independence, traffic-weighting, delayed-label, and preregistration limitations remain.
model: Use nonpreemptive latest-pending coalescing for asynchronous FIFO monitor workers. Running checks finish; whenever all workers are busy, a new checkpoint replaces the older queued checkpoint. Skipped looks leave alpha unused, and a monotone confidence-threshold gate verifies that the next processed look after a dropped crossing remains statistically sufficient.

validation.alpha_validity: Coalescing depends only on look arrival and worker state, not monitor outcomes; skipped looks leave their alpha unspent.
validation.fifo_dominance: Across every integer service cost from zero through the exact scan, coalesced per-schedule action cost is no greater than FIFO.
validation.synchronous_bound: Every coalesced action cost is no greater than E76's synchronous blocking upper bound.
validation.zero_service_control: Every worker policy exactly reproduces FIFO per-case oracle action cost at zero service.
